column2: The head of a monastery, a leader whose household lives by the timetable of prayers.
The one at the wheel of a car, responsible for the passengers arriving rather than getting acquainted with the ditch.
A stretch of text between two indented lines; a small breathing space for the eye and the thought.
A medical termination of pregnancy.
A person outside the law, often in hiding in the mountains or in the forests.
The outer contour of an object, or a brief sketch of its shape; a silhouette without the details.
Part of a wage or payment handed over early; money that arrives before the work is done.
Urgent work under severe time pressure; everything that needed doing yesterday.
A large public-transport vehicle that gathers passengers along its route like a collector.
A means of transport with an engine, four wheels and a perpetual need for parking.
The creator of a book, article or other work; the one who receives both the glory and the editor's corrections.
A southern plant with fleshy leaves, like a green rosette with a mind of its own.
A gelling substance from seaweed; the plant-based helper of jellies and desserts.
A semi-precious stone with bands and patterns that nature painted without a brush.
A follower of a teaching or idea; a person not merely curious, but already enrolled in the club of the convinced.
The precise instruction of where to deliver a letter, a parcel or the long-awaited courier.
The keenness that makes one keep playing even after the words 'last round'.
An inhabitant or member of the peoples of Asia.
The chemical element making up most of the Earth's atmosphere; the invisible companion of every breath.
A long-legged bird with a long bill whom popular rumour appointed the delivery service of babies.
An aromatic yellow fruit with firm flesh; stubborn when raw, magnificent in jam.
The long branch of a nerve cell along which the signal travels to other cells.
A person who can live several other lives in an afternoon — and collects applause for it.
A path lined with trees; a promenade corridor in the open air.
A horse's manner of moving — walk, trot or gallop; its very own transport mode.
The hardest natural mineral; once cut, it becomes a cut diamond and an object of longing.
A medicinal plant with soft leaves and a root used in apothecary remedies — and the ancestor of the sweet of the same name.
A tart — occasionally ferociously tart — relative of the plum, excellent for sauces and jam.
A farm building for storing grain and supplies; the larder at rural scale.
A rare aromatic substance associated with sperm whales and perfumery; the sea's mystery in a flacon, priced accordingly.
The unit of electric current; the answer to how briskly the charges are moving.
The Roman god of love, who prefers arrows to diplomacy.
A large roofed hall for aircraft, machinery or substantial equipment.
A heavenly messenger with wings in painting and a reputation as a keeper in everyday speech.
A negatively charged ion; a particle with more electrons than neutrality.
The electrode at which oxidation occurs in an electrochemical system; one of the electrodes in a vacuum tube — not to be confused with the cathode.
A brief preliminary message about an event still gathering itself to happen.
The fluid of a car's cooling system that keeps the engine unfrozen in winter.
The body's largest artery, through which blood leaves the heart for the greater circulation.
A member of a large Semitic people of the Middle East and North Africa; the word denotes belonging to a broad linguistic and cultural community.
A large striped fruit with red flesh; the summer treat that resists being eaten tidily.
An inert noble gas; almost nobody gets into a chemical relationship with it.
The territory over which an animal or plant species is found; a species' natural address.
The stage for a circus act, a sporting contest or a public struggle for attention.
A legal measure restricting liberty; the moment when the evening's plans change abruptly.
A solo vocal number in opera, when the hero finally gets the spotlight — and the orchestra.
A curved structure or doorway; the builder's way of passing gracefully from one space into another.
A long rope with a sliding loop for catching cattle; the classic cowboy's tool.
A state's armed forces; the organisation where discipline outranks the personal timetable.
A stringed instrument with a triangular frame; it looks like a staircase for the fingers.
The place where documents outlast the memory of why they were created.
A chronic condition of the airways whose attacks of difficult breathing call for medical attention.
The autumn flower shaped like a star, adorning the beds when summer is already packing its bags.
A determined advance on an opponent; in sport and games, the push to turn defence into a result.
A car with a driver who, for payment, takes the passenger wherever the passenger has named in the app.
A sportsman of developed strength and endurance; a person for whom dumbbells are nearly household items.
The Earth's gaseous envelope; figuratively, the mood of a place, felt before a word is spoken.
A ring-shaped coral island around a lagoon; a tropical scene built by very small sea builders.
An insect with bright wings that began life as a caterpillar, in no apparent hurry to transform.
The smallest particle of a chemical element to keep its properties; the building block of matter.
A small rural settlement, often nestled in the hills or mountains.
An invisible energy field, according to certain teachings; in ordinary speech, a particular impression.
In sport, the state of the ball or player beyond the field of play; the short word that stops the game.
A fraudulent or risky scheme in which the promises are usually noticeably prettier than the result.
A placard or notice of a play, concert or other event; the cultural hint of where to spend the evening.
A member of the ancient people of central Mexico, who built a powerful state before the Spanish arrived.
The mother of one of your parents; the family member whose tea and care arrive unrequested — and never take no for an answer.
A traveller's cases and bags; all the necessities that are mysteriously heavier on the way home.
A long French loaf with a crisp crust; the symbol of the bakery that barely fits into an ordinary shopping bag.
A long pole with a metal hook on the end, for pulling in or holding objects.
An ornamental and medicinal plant with large leathery leaves and pink flower clusters.
A large wooden or metal vessel for water; a bucket grown ambitious.
A foundation, a strongpoint or a place of stationing; the thing without which building and planning struggle to start.
An eastern market of trading rows, noise, smells and the art of haggling.
A ceremonial evening of dancing, fine clothes, music and the rules of polite society.
A ballet artist who turns physically demanding work into the appearance of weightlessness.
Theatrical art in which the story is told by movement, music and pointe shoes instead of ordinary lines.
A long sweet tropical fruit in a yellow skin; a convenient snack until the skin becomes a trap.
An organised group of criminals; a collective whose corporate culture clearly leaves much to be desired.
A paper money token; the compact reminder that purchases are rarely free.
A craft with a jet engine; it can put a satellite into orbit, or a firework into the sky.
A decoration of ribbon with loops and a knot; the simple way to make a gift look festive.
The place where one steams, washes and emerges renewed — at least in one's own estimation.
A plain, long building for temporary or communal living; architecture with no frills.
A poet who sings their own songs to their own accompaniment; verse that needs no orchestra.
A chemical element of the alkaline earth metals; its compounds serve, among other things, in X-ray diagnostics.
A heavy mineral, barium sulphate, used in industry; a stone of very solid weight.
A sailing vessel of several masts, square-rigged on the fore masts and fore-and-aft on the last.
A flat-bottomed river craft for carrying goods; the water haulage of former times.
A hereditary noble title; the step of the aristocratic ladder below the count.
A large predatory cat with a spotted coat, equally at home in trees and tall grass.
A short instructive tale, often with animals in the leading roles and a moral at the close.
A starchy root of tropical origin; a kitchen relative of the potato, though not a botanical one.
An oblong white bread; the faithful companion of soup, sandwiches and sudden hunger.
A springy platform for jumping, turning an ordinary bounce into a sport in its own right.
A large soft travel bag; the container of things that 'may come in handy'.
A tall narrow structure, visible from afar; the architectural way of seeing the world from above.
A tree with white bark; a familiar figure of the northern landscape and one of Britain's prettiest natives.
Movement in quick steps, with both feet periodically off the ground.
An athlete, or simply a person who travels at a run; sometimes the one fleeing trouble.
The upper part of the leg from hip to knee; in anatomy, the region containing the femur.
A small marsh bird with a long straight bill and a characteristic zigzag flight, much admired by British sportsmen.
Salted or smoked pork with alternating meat and fat; the aromatic argument for breakfast.
A churchgoer without monastic vows; an ordinary member of the flock, not of the cloister.
A nimble woodland creature with a bushy tail, storing nuts in the manner of a seasoned storekeeper.
The edge of land at a river, lake or sea; where the water ends and the firm ground begins.
A soft round head covering without a peak; the accessory of artists, soldiers and devotees of the French look.
A building mixture of cement, water and aggregate that sets into the foundation of buildings and bridges.
A temporary open-air encampment for hikers, campers or soldiers.
A metal vessel with a lid and handle for milk; the village container with a distinctive ring — and a star of the dairy doorstep.
Activity pursued for profit; the art of turning an idea, labour and risk into a monetary result.
An entrepreneur who organises the undertaking, takes the decisions and tries to make the numbers add up.
A large wild ox of North America, with a massive head and thick fur at the front.
A document or electronic proof of the right to travel, enter or take part; the pass to the event in question.
A draft law or legislative act of the English-speaking tradition; a document with a political route still to travel.
An unauthorised military absence from duty or barracks without permission.
A reddish-orange, malleable metal prized for its exceptional conductivity — and for making pennies and wires.
